html:
In 2022 Sri Lanka ran out of foreign money, failed to pay its debts for the first time, and saw its president chased from office by crowds.

The country had borrowed heavily abroad for years to build ports, roads and an airport. Several blows then fell together. Large tax cuts in 2019 emptied the treasury. Bombings that year and then Covid stopped the tourists. In April 2021 the president, Gotabaya Rajapaksa, banned chemical fertiliser overnight, and the rice and tea harvests fell.

By early 2022 there was no money to import fuel, cooking gas or medicine. Power was cut for up to thirteen hours a day, and people queued for days at petrol stations. Prices rose by about 70 per cent in a year. In April the government stopped paying its foreign debt.

A protest camp grew outside the president's office in Colombo. It called itself the Aragalaya, "the struggle", and it drew Sinhalese, Tamils and Muslims together. The Rajapaksa family had ruled for most of twenty years and had won the civil war. The prime minister, the president's brother, resigned in May. On 9 July crowds walked into the president's house and swam in his pool. He fled abroad and resigned by email.

A loan from the International Monetary Fund followed. In 2024 voters chose a left-wing outsider as president.
sum: In 2022 Sri Lanka ran out of foreign money, failed to pay its debts for the first time, and saw its president chased from office by crowds.
